newsitem.title: USA: Vitro's Anchor Glass sold for $365 mln.
newsitem.headline: Vitro's Anchor Glass sold for $365 mln.

text.p: Vitro SA's Anchor Glass Container Corp said on Friday that it has completed a definitive agreement to sell its assets to Ball-Foster Glass Container Co LLC for $365 million in cash and the assumption of certain liabilities.
The transaction must be approved by the bankruptcy court and regulatory authorities. It is scheduled to close by the end of this year.
The board of directors has appointed Anchor Chairman James Malone acting president of the company. Anchor President and Chief Executive Alfonso Palacio has resigned effective immediately.

Ball-Foster, a producer of glass containers based in Muncie, Ind., is 42 percent owned by Ball Corp, a container company and 58 percent owned by French glass container company Compagnie de Saint-Gobain.

Meanwhile, Anchor Glass said in a separate statement that it has filed a complaint with the U.S. Bankruptcy Court in Wilmington, Delaware, seeking an order to block the prosecution of a complaint filed by Owens-Brockway Glass Container Inc.

Owens-Brockway had sought damages and an injunction preventing Ball-Foster from purchasing assets that allegedly contain trade secrets and properietary information provided to Anchor by Owens-Brockway. Anchor contended Owens-Brockway's actions are an attempt to interfere with the sale of the company.
